To achieve consistency with the eligibility rules of publicly funded programs for cash grants, nutrition
assistance, health care, and legal services (OAR 461-110-210 and 461-110-370 may provide additional
context for these determinations),
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT Multnomah County Trial Court Administration staff making initial
determinations regarding eligibility for fee waivers and fee deferrals for court costs shall supplement the
definition of "household" adopted by Chief Justice Order 10-045 dated August 26, 2010, ('"Household'
means a person or group of people occupying a common dwelling and sharing necessary living
expenses") with the following:
"Sharing necessary living expenses" includes but is not limited to situations in which persons occupying a
common dwelling customarily purchase and prepare meals together. A single dwelling may contain more
than one household, each functioning as a single financial unit whose members share living expenses.
When the party requesting a fee deferral or waiver is adverse to a party named in the action for which fees
are required, those parties are presumed to no longer share necessary living expenses."
. IT IS HEREBY FURTHER ORDERED THAT when considering a party's fee wai¥e!".Of-deferral.petitiott---­to
file an action or for an appearance in an action, in actions other than domestic relations cases, the
income of the adverse party shall not be a factor in determining whether the petitioning party is granted a
waiver or deferral.
Nothing in this order restricts any judge from re-examining an earlier determination of a petition for a fee
waiver or deferral, and setting aside the earlier order based on current information concerning the ability
of the petitioning party, or any party to the action in which the petition for a deferral or waiver was filed,
to satisfy the petitioner's fee obligation as provided under law and subject to an appropriate order of the
court.
